summary: The Nasdaq bounced but could not reclaim the line that broke. NQ closed 29,177, up 0.29 percent and still below its stop and 50-average, while the S&P closed red at 7,672. Gold kept unwinding to 4,009 and crude was the standout, up 4.38 percent to 103.43. VIX held near 19.5 into next week's Fed meeting.

event.actual: A failed equity bounce. The Nasdaq rallied off the open but closed below its stop and 50-average, the S&P closed red, gold kept unwinding, and crude ran on its own supply story.
event.surprise: The Nasdaq led the bounce yet the S&P closed red, so breadth was weaker than the headline tape. Crude detached from stocks with a 4.38 percent gain.
event.nqReaction: NQ broke its opening range up at 13:45 UTC, ran to 29,325, then faded to close 29,177, up 0.29 percent, still below stop and EMA50.
event.crossAsset: MES minus 0.41 percent at 7,672.25. December gold minus 0.75 percent at 4,009.5. December crude plus 4.38 percent at 103.43. VIX 19.45, up 2.21 percent.

risk.openRisk: Flat to light. No new index longs until price reclaims its stop.
risk.note: The Fed meeting is next week, Oct 27 to 28. Keep size small into it and avoid new index longs until price reclaims its stop. The long-only momentum edge is blocked below the 50-average. Crude is the one clean trend-long, above its 101.61 stop, with January now on MCL2!. VIX near 19.5 keeps both sides live.

psychology: A bounce that cannot reclaim the line that broke is a pullback inside a downtrend, so treat it that way. Today the Nasdaq rallied hard off the open and still closed under its stop and its average. If you bought the pop, the takeaway is to wait for acceptance back above the broken level before you trust the turn. One strong hour is not a reclaim. Let price prove it with two closes, then think about size.
